steps.title: Check Safety
steps.content: Ensure the scene is safe for you and the victim. Do not put yourself in danger.

steps.title: Check Responsiveness
steps.content: Tap the victim's shoulder and shout 'Are you okay?'. If no response, call emergency services immediately.

steps.title: Start Chest Compressions
steps.content: Place the heel of one hand on the center of the chest. Place the other hand on top. Push hard and fast (100-120 beats per minute).

steps.title: Rescue Breaths
steps.content: If trained, give 2 rescue breaths after every 30 compressions. Otherwise, continue hands-only CPR until help arrives.

steps.title: Apply Pressure
steps.content: Apply direct pressure to the wound using a clean cloth or gauze. Keep applying pressure continuously.

steps.title: Elevate
steps.content: If possible, raise the injured area above the level of the heart to slow bleeding.

steps.title: Bandage
steps.content: Once bleeding fits, wrap the wound tightly with a bandage. If blood soaks through, add more layers—do not remove the first layer.

steps.title: Cool the Burn
steps.content: Hold the burned area under cool (not cold) running water for at least 10-20 minutes. Do not use ice.

steps.title: Remove Constrictions
steps.content: Remove rings, watches, or tight clothing around the burn before swelling starts.

steps.title: Cover
steps.content: Cover the burn with a clean, non-stick bandage or plastic wrap. Do not apply creams or butter.

steps.title: Encourage Coughing
steps.content: If the person can cough, encourage them to keep coughing.

steps.title: Back Blows
steps.content: If they cannot breathe, lean them forward and give 5 sharp back blows between the shoulder blades.

steps.title: Abdominal Thrusts
steps.content: If back blows fail, stand behind them and perform 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver). Repeat cycle.

steps.title: Check Breathing
steps.content: Tilt head back and lift chin. Look, listen, and feel for breathing for no more than 10 seconds.

steps.title: Recovery Position
steps.content: If breathing, place them on their side (recovery position) to keep airway open.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.content: Stay with them and keep checking breathing until help arrives.

steps.title: Immobilize
steps.content: Keep the injured area still. Support it with a splint if available.

steps.title: Cold Compress
steps.content: Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth for 10 minutes to reduce swelling.

steps.title: Treat for Shock
steps.content: Help them lie down comfortably. Cover with a blanket to keep warm.
